entries.agenda_title: Downlink control channel, scheduling for downlink and uplink transmission
entries.text: Study the adaptation of the number of Rx antennas for PDCCH monitoring in 6GR for UE energy efficiency purpose, including at least energy saving gain, impact to coverage, impact to PDCCH blocking, spec impacts, how to ensure common understanding between UE and NW, application delay of antenna adaptation, impact to PDSCH reception.

entries.agenda_title: Downlink control channel, scheduling for downlink and uplink transmission
entries.text:
Study at least the following mechanisms for DCI Container size determinations at least for RRC connected state
- A DCI Container (defined for discussion purpose) is the physical payload that the UE attempts for decoding with a given size
  - no size alignment procedures across different DCI containers
- Alt 1: The DCI container size is implicitly determined by RRC for the DCI container, e.g., possible contents of the DCI
- Alt 2: The network explicitly configures DCI container size(s) via RRC
- Alt 3: DCI container size is pre-defined without any dependency on RRC
Note: the above studies are applicable for single-stage DCI and two-stage DCI
FFS: additional alternatives applicable for two-stage DCI only
FFS: maximum number of DCI container sizes for a UE
FFS: whether/how to do padding/truncation within a DCI container
ffs: FFS: additional alternatives applicable for two-stage DCI only
FFS: maximum number of DCI container sizes for a UE
FFS: whether/how to do padding/truncation within a DCI container

entries.agenda_title: Downlink control channel, scheduling for downlink and uplink transmission
entries.text:
For the study of two-stage DCI in 6GR, consider at least the following options for the physical channels/signals for the two stages:
- Option 1: PDCCH for both the 1st stage and 2nd stage(s), and the 2nd stage(s) use the same transmission scheme and physical resource structure as the 1st stage
- Option 2: PDCCH for the 1st stage,
  - Dedicated time/frequency domain resource for the 2nd stage(s) is indicated in the 1st stage
  - The 2nd stage(s) use a different transmission scheme and/or physical resource structure from the 1st stage
    - FFS the physical channel for the 2nd stage and how the 2nd stage is transmitted over the indicated resource
- Option 3: PDCCH for the 1st stage, and
  - If the [2nd stage/two-stage] DCI schedules PDSCH(s) carrying DL-SCH data,
    - 2nd stage is multiplexed on PDSCH(s) with DL-SCH data
      - The 1st stage indicates the time/frequency domain resource for the PDSCH(s) with DL-SCH data
      - FFS how the multiplexing is done
  - If the [2nd stage/two-stage] DCI does not schedule any PDSCH carrying DL-SCH data,
    - Option 3-1: Same as Option 1
    - Option 3-2: Same as Option 2
- Option 4: sequence for the 1st stage, PDCCH for the 2nd stage
  - Note: this is different from WUS-based PDCCH monitoring adaptation at least in the sense that whenever a two-stage DCI is transmitted, both the sequence and the 2nd stage PDCCH are always transmitted, i.e., there is a one-to-one correspondence between the 1st stage and 2nd stage.
  - Note: deprioritize the sequence design until more detailed design of Option 4 is available.
  - FFS: FAR and MDR target for the sequence
- Note: Polar coding is assumed except for the 1st stage in Option 4.
ffs: FFS the physical channel for the 2nd stage and how the 2nd stage is transmitted over the indicated resource
FFS how the multiplexing is done
FFS: FAR and MDR target for the sequence

entries.agenda_title: Downlink control channel, scheduling for downlink and uplink transmission
entries.text:
For the study of two-stage DCI in 6GR, consider the following options for the information carried in the two stages:
- Option A
  - 1st stage DCI
    - Carry only the information to decode the 2nd stage DCI
  - 2nd stage DCI
    - Carry scheduling info for PDSCH(s)/PUSCH(s) and/or other downlink control information (e.g., same as single stage DCI)
- Option B
  - 1st stage DCI
    - Carry the information to decode the 2nd stage DCI and part of {scheduling info for PDSCH(s)/PUSCH(s) and/or other downlink control information}
  - 2nd stage DCI
    - Carry additional {scheduling info for PDSCH(s)/PUSCH(s) and/or other downlink control information} on top of those in 1st stage DCI
- Option C
  - 1st stage: a sequence indicating at least the presence of the 2nd stage DCI and/or the information to decode the 2nd stage
  - 2nd stage DCI: same as a single-stage DCI
  - Note: this option is applicable to only Option 4 of the physical channels/signals for the two stages
- Other options are not precluded.
- Note: companies are encouraged to analyse pros/cons of above options compared with single stage DCI

For the study on the ambiguity between DTX of DL assignment and PDSCH decoding failure in the HARQ-ACK codebook for 6GR, consider at least:
  - NW implementation based approach including impacts on UEs with different NW implementation if any, impact of DTX events (e.g., assuming PDCCH missed detection probability is 1%)
  - Self-decodable and non-self decodable PDSCH
  - Trade-off between additional feedback overhead and performance benefits

For DL HARQ in 6GR, support HARQ-ACK information bits transmitted via L1 signalling (i.e., Mechanism 1).
- The design of DL HARQ-ACK feedback operation allows at least the possibility for the following while ensuring HARQ-ACK performance
  - Relaxing the need for tight coordination between schedulers (e.g., between multiple carriers, between DL and UL, etc.)
    - Decoupling of HARQ-ACK feedback triggering from the DL assignments scheduling the corresponding PDSCH
    - Other solution that addresses the same issue can also be considered
  - Other factors can also be considered
- The design of DL HARQ-ACK feedback operation allows the simplification of UL channel collision/multiplexing/transmission (e.g., resource determination) involving HARQ-ACK

Study HARQ-ACK codebook(s) for downlink HARQ operation in 6GR, considering:
- HARQ-ACK codebook based on NR Type-1, NR Type-2, or NR (enhanced) Type-3 as starting point

In 6GR, for the study of downlink HARQ-ACK feedback granularity smaller than TB-level and corresponding mechanism, consider at least the following:
- XOR-based retransmission feedback
- CB/CBG-level HARQ-ACK feedback of high-probability error patterns
- NR CBG HARQ-ACK feedback
- Codebook-based feedback
- Two-stage feedback
- 2D lattice-based CBs feedback
- Per-PDSCH on demand request of CBG-level feedback
- Mixture of TB-level and CBG-level feedback
- Non-uniform CB-to-CBG mapping feedback
- HARQ-ACK feedback enabling/disabling for some of CBGs
- enabling/disabling of CBG-level HARQ-ACK feedback
- Separate HARQ-ACK for CBs that carry MAC CEs or similar important data
Note: in the above applicable options, CB-level and CBG-level can be both considered.
Note: For the evaluation of above options, consider at least (average) feedback overhead per TB, ratio between size of retransmitted CB(s)/CBG(s) and size of original TB, and impact on DL control overhead, considering practical setup (e.g., fading channel, correlation across CBs, link adaptation, etc.)
Note: Companies are encouraged to check FL summary and contributions

For Method 3 (Next available/feasible time slot of semi-static configured resources that satisfy UE processing time/capability), study details of the following:
- NW configures periodic UL feedback resources/timing occasions and UE feedback HARQ-ACK information for a PDSCH and/or a PDCCH associated with HARQ-ACK feedback received before a deadline in the first available UL feedback resource/timing occasion, where the deadline is determined/configured/indicated subject to UE processing time (e.g., Tproc,1) before the UL feedback resource/timing occasion.
Note: all 5G NR terminologies used are for discussion purpose only

For Method 1 (dynamic indication of HARQ-ACK feedback timing and resource in DCI), study details of at least the following:
- The HARQ-ACK feedback timing and/or resource is indicated in
  - each DL DCI with/without scheduling corresponding PDSCH(s) with associated HARQ-ACK feedback
    - the DCI can provide
        - indication of HARQ-ACK feedback timing and/or resource with applicable values for HARQ-ACK transmission;
        - indication of HARQ-ACK feedback timing and/or resource can be invalid or absent (e.g., NNK1, non-numeric PRI, no field(s))
  - an UL DCI,
  - a dedicated DCI triggering HARQ-ACK feedback,
  - a DL DCI that schedules a PDSCH not associated with that HARQ-ACK feedback, and/or
  - other DCI
  - If the DL DCI indicates an invalid timing and/or resource or timing and/or resource are absent, then the HARQ-ACK feedback timing and/or resource is determined by one of the above or other methods
  - FFS: multiple HARQ-ACK feedback resources for multiple PDSCHs
Note: all 5G NR terminologies used are for discussion purpose only
ffs: FFS: multiple HARQ-ACK feedback resources for multiple PDSCHs

entries.agenda_title: Other physical layer signals, channels and procedure
entries.text:
RAN1 to evaluate the BSR in CB PUSCH, considering at least the following aspects:
- The performance of decoding a PUSCH payload when N UEs transmit in the one same time and frequency PUSCH resource with considering the following assumptions:
  - The N UEs use N different DMRS ports from a common pool of M (N<= M) different DMRS ports.
  - The N UEs use same DMRS port from a common pool of M (N <= M) different DMRS ports but with different scrambling IDs for DMRS sequence.
  - The N UEs use different combinations of DMRS port and scrambling ID for DMRS sequence, where the DMRS port(s) are chosen from a common pool of M(N<=M) different DMRS ports.
  - The N UEs could use same or different waveform for PUSCH transmission.
  - The N UEs use the same DMRS port from a common pool of M (N <= M) different DMRS ports and same scrambling IDs for DMRS sequence
- Evaluate the following aspects of CB-BSR:
  - Study and identify the definition of UE collision in CB PUSCH used for this evaluation and evaluate the probability of UE collision.
    - Companies to report the definition used in their evaluations
  - The L1 transmission delay of BSR in CB PUSCH.
    - The L1 transmission delay is the time duration between the traffic arrival and when the BSR is decoded successfully.
  - The CDF of the number of attempts of BSR transmission.
  - The complexity of blind detection at the BS side.
    - The evaluation can take into account that UEs uses C-RNTI or common RNTI for PUSCH scrambling and/or the number of different DMRS that is detected.
  - The UL resource overhead for transmitting CB BSR.
  - The impact of DMRS false alarm (if any).
  - The above study and evaluation can consider system load.

entries.agenda_title: Other physical layer signals, channels and procedure
entries.text:
Study L1 multi-bit SR with considering the following aspects:
- The reporting contents for corresponding transmission condition in SR,
- Identify the benefit and necessity of multi-bit SR over 1-bit SR:
  - at least considering the latency of PUSCH resource scheduling, trade-off between SR overhead and accuracy of UL resource scheduling/buffer status information compression.
- The potential required bit size of a multi-bit SR for each candidate reporting content.
- The uplink channel for conveying multi-bit SR.
- Compare multi-bit SR with other solutions.
- The 1-bit SR+BSR mechanism is the benchmark for study.

entries.agenda_title: Other physical layer signals, channels and procedure
entries.text:
For UE-to-UE CLI measurement and reporting in 6GR:
- RAN1 to study the following metrics for UE-to-UE CLI measurements:
  - RSSI and RSRP for direct interference, e.g., intra-band or intra-subband CLI.
  - RSSI to measure the leakage of the interference, e.g., inter-subband CLI.
  - The frequency domain granularity for measurement to be considered are: subband and wideband.
- RAN1 to study the following methods of CLI measurement resources:
  - CLI measurement based on explicit configuration of CLI RSSI measurement resource and/or SRS for RSRP measurement.
  - CLI measurement/detection without explicit measurement resource configuration, e.g., exploit PDSCH reception to measure/detect CLI.
- Study network-controlled CLI reporting.
  - The benefits/drawbacks of network-controlled CLI reporting.
  - The reporting signalling and triggering mechanisms.
  - Study the following candidate reporting contents:
    - Option 1: N strongest RSRP or RSSI and corresponding resource indicators.
      - Report RSRP/RSSI for the strongest one and differential RSRP/RSSI for the other N-1.
    - Option 2: indication of whether each measurement resource has RSRP or RSSI measurement larger than a threshold, for example one bitmap with each bit corresponding to one measurement resource.
    - and any other options.
- Study UE-initiated/event-triggering CLI reporting for overhead reduction and energy saving, at least considering the following aspects:
  - The benefits over the network-controlled reporting.
  - The definition of CLI event and study how to trigger the CLI reporting.
  - The measurement resource/occasions for UE to detect the CLI event.
  - The reporting contents and the UL reporting mechanism.
- For the time alignment issue of CLI measurement resource:
  - Study the reference timing that is used for each associated measurement occasions.
  - Study whether/how the time alignment issue has impact on CLI measurement performance.
  - Study the methods to handle the time alignment, if necessary

entries.agenda_title: Other physical layer signals, channels and procedure
entries.text:
For BS-to-BS CLI measurement in 6GR:
- RAN1 recommends to use CSI-RS and synchronization signal (e.g., 6GR SSB) to measure BS-to-BS CLI or Channel.
  - Further study other channel or RS used for measuring BS-to-BS CLI.
- Study UL resource muting mechanism for handling BS-to-BS in 6GR
  - The UL resource muting mechanism specified in 5G/NR is the baseline for study.
  - Study both transparent and non-transparent UL resource muting mechanisms,
  - Study the mechanism with flexible UL resource muting symbol position(s) and flexible disable/enable indication.
  - Study UL resource muting pattern.
- Study the information exchange between the BSs, at least including the configuration of the CSI-RS and synchronization signal, measurement results, the recommended beam index and non-recommended beam index, the TDD time/frequency resources configuration, the SBFD time/frequency resources configuration.

entries.agenda_title: Design of WUS with OFDM based sequence
entries.text:
- The False Alarm Rate is defined as the rate with which the UE detects any targeting DL WUS sequence, given that no DL WUS sequence was transmitted.
- The False Detection Rate is defined as the rate with which the UE detects any targeting DL WUS sequence, given that any different DL WUS sequence(s) was transmitted.

Study for DL WUS coverage, considering, e.g., by

Study at least the following sequence families for 6GR DL WUS design,
- Zadoff-Chu sequences, or its variants

at least with respect to,
- Link level performance (MDR, FAR, FDR), including time and frequency errors

For the paging rate per PO for evaluation purpose, assume per UE paging rate as RE, REF= 1%, 0.1%, 0.01% or 0.001% and YREF = 1.28s, and group paging rate RG can be determined as below:

entries.text:
For intra-frequency neighboring cell RRM measurement for RRC idle and RRC connected by EE processing, study at least
- RRM measurement by EE processing, including at least
- How to perform neighboring cell measurement, considering timeline and the number of neighboring cells
- Whether/how to limit the applicable cases: synchronous case only or both synchronous case and asynchronous case
- Cell detection/identification (if applicable), is performed by:

entries.text:
For 6G NTN, RAN1 to evaluate solutions for satellite having more beam footprints than simultaneously active beams by reporting the following for a given combination of {hierarchical beam structure scheme, default SSB periodicity}:
- Coverage ratio for common channels, obtained as per Rel-19 methodology as (N2/(N1 + N2)) assuming N3=0.
- Resource overhead of common channels.
- Impact on link budget and cell acquisition latency (e.g. for a single sync raster point).
- Impact (from RAN1 perspective) on measurements
- NOTE: Details on assumptions for this evaluation (e.g. percentage of simultaneous active beams for UL and DL, calculation of cell acquisition latency, link budget, what common channels and their configuration are included for the resource overhead, etc.) will be separately discussed, and can be reported by companies until RAN1 can reach an agreement.
- Companies to report details on the proposed hierarchical beam structure scheme and default SSB periodicity, including at least:
  - Details on hierarchical beam structure scheme include at least the following:
    - Assumed beam structure (e.g. wide/narrow beam, including the assumed beamwidth for the different beams), for both UL and DL.
    - What channels / signals are transmitted in the different beams.
    - Peak EIRP / antenna gain of the different beams
    - Beam illumination pattern for the different beams (e.g. TDM between wide/narrow beam)
    - Methodology for calculation of N1/N2
  - Details on default SSB periodicity include at least the following:
    - Beam illumination scheme for different signals / channels.
    - SSB periodicity value.
- NOTE: The above does not imply that hierarchical beam structure is only relevant for cases where the satellite has more beam footprints than simultaneously active beams
- NOTE: Structure of NR signals / channels can be initially used for evaluation until other agenda items progress on the 6GR signals / channel structure.
NOTE: The Rel-19 agreement including the definition of N1/N2/N3 is as follows:
| For system level study based on analytical evaluation: N1 beam footprints are in state “off” These beam footprints are not served by any signal (no satellite service in this area) N2 beam footprints are in state “common messages only” These beam footprints do not have any active user traffic, and are served the necessary information for cell discovery and initial access. Optionally, companies may consider user arrival (e.g. RACH access) in this type of cell, and should describe how this is taken into account in the analytical evaluation N3 beam footprints are in state “active traffic” These beam footprints have X active (e.g. VoNR) users each. These beam footprints are also served the necessary information for cell discovery and initial access N1 + N2 + N3 = “Total number of beam footprints “ N1, N2, N3, X are to be reported by companies. Resource utilization obtained under the assumptions above is to be reported by companies. Other assumptions made in the evaluation are to be reported by companies, e.g. power sharing scheme, beam hopping scheme, etc. |

For object detection and/or tracking, define velocity accuracy for 6G ISAC evaluation:
Velocity accuracy is defined as the absolute value of the difference between the estimated velocity and the corresponding true velocity of a sensing target. For single node monostatic sensing or single pair of bistatic sensing, both the radial velocity accuracy and the 3D velocity accuracy can be estimated. The true radial velocity is the sum of the following two components:
- Component 1: The projection of the velocity difference vector on the unit-norm vector from target to STX, where the velocity difference vector is between the true 3D velocity of the target and the true 3D velocity of the STX;
- Component 2: The projection of the velocity difference vector on the unit-norm vector from target to SRX, where the velocity difference vector is between the true 3D velocity of the target and the true 3D velocity of the SRX.
Note: If STx and SRx are static, true radial velocity is , where  is the true 3D velocity of the target,  is the bistatic angle between incident direction and scattering direction, and  is the angle between the true 3D velocity vector and the bisector vector within the bistatic angle . For Rel-20 6G ISAC evaluation on communication assistance, the following SAC (sensing assisted communication) evaluation scope is considered:
- Further discuss the sensing measurement/result used to assist communication, which may include, e.g.:
  - Delay/Doppler/angle/power/phase related information of the ISAC channel
  - Information of detected objects (static or moving) and/or large size surface (e.g. EO type-2)
- Further discuss evaluation of the performance of sensing measurement/results, which are used to assist communication.
  - Scenario: At least Urban Grid is considered
    - Urban Grid with or without EO type-2 can both be considered
    - Other scenarios are not precluded.
  - FFS detailed evaluation assumptions, sensing modes, prior information of EO-type2, etc.
  - When evaluated, company should report:
    - Performance metrics on sensing measurement/result used to assist communication
    - How such sensing measurement/result is able to assist the communication
    - The corresponding performance of sensing measurement/results
- Further discuss evaluation of communication performance assisted by sensing.
  - SAC use cases that observed in AI 10.8.2 can be considered
  - When evaluated, company should use the same scenario/assumptions (and ISAC channel if applicable) as sensing performance evaluation.
  - When evaluated, company should clarify whether ideal/non-ideal sensing measurement/result is used to assist communication.
  - When evaluated, company should report:
    - Communication-related performance metrics
    - Detailed methods on how the sensing measurements/results assist the communication
    - The corresponding communication performance gain/loss
Note: Strive for minimizing/no extension on existing channel model. It is up to company to use chapter 7/8 of TR38.901 for communication performance evaluation.

| 5.2.1.6 CSI processing criteria ============================= unchanged parts are omitted ============================ For a CSI report with CSI-ReportConfig with higher layer parameter reportQuantity not set to 'none', or a CSI report with LTM-CSI-ReportConfig, or reportQuantity not set to 'none-bm-r19' or 'none-csi-r19', the CPU(s) (including and/or , for CSI reports with reportQuantity set to 'p-cri-r19', 'p-cri-RSRP-r19', 'p-ssb-index-r19', or 'p-ssb-index-RSRP-r19', and CSI reports configured with the higher layer parameter csi-InferencePrediction-r19, and for CSI report with reportQuantity set to 'rs-pai-r19' or 'csi-pai-r19') are occupied for a number of OFDM symbols as follows: - A periodic or semi-persistent CSI report (excluding an initial semi-persistent CSI report on PUSCH after the PDCCH triggering the report, a semi-persistent CSI report on PUSCH configured with reportQuantity set to 'csi-pai-r19', and a semi-persistent CSI report on PUSCH configured with the higher layer parameter codebookType set to 'typeII-Doppler-r18' or 'typeII-Doppler-PortSelection-r18') occupies CPU(s) from the first symbol of the earliest one of each CSI-RS/CSI-IM/SSB resource, or each CSI-RS/CSI-IM resource associated with all configured sub-configurations for periodic CSI report corresponding to a CSI-ReportConfig that contains a list of sub-configurations provided by csi-ReportSubConfigToAddModList, or each CSI-RS/CSI-IM resource associated with all activated/triggered sub-configurations for semi-persistent CSI report corresponding to a CSI-ReportConfig that contains a list of sub-configurations provided by csi-ReportSubConfigToAddModList, for channel or interference measurement, respective latest CSI-RS/CSI-IM/SSB occasion no later than the corresponding CSI reference resource, until the last symbol of the configured PUSCH/PUCCH carrying the report. - An aperiodic CSI report occupies CPU(s) from the first symbol after the PDCCH triggering the CSI report until the last symbol of the scheduled PUSCH carrying the report. When the PDCCH reception includes two PDCCH candidates from two respective search space sets, as described in clause 10.1 of [6, TS 38.213], for the purpose of determining the CPU occupation duration, the PDCCH candidate that ends later in time is used. - An initial semi-persistent CSI report on PUSCH after the PDCCH trigger occupies CPU(s) from the first symbol after the PDCCH until the last symbol of the scheduled PUSCH carrying the report. When the PDCCH reception includes two PDCCH candidates from two respective search space sets, as described in clause 10.1 of [6, TS 38.213], for the purpose of determining the CPU occupation duration, the PDCCH candidate that ends later in time is used. - A semi-persistent CSI report on PUSCH configured with the higher layer parameter codebookType set to 'typeII-Doppler-r18' or 'typeII-Doppler-PortSelection-r18' occupies CPU(s) from the first symbol of KP-th latest consecutive periodic/semi-persistent CSI-RS occasions no later than CSI reference resource, until the last symbol of the PUSCH carrying the report, where the value of is indicated by UE capability. - A semi-persistent CSI report on PUSCH configured with reportQuantity set to 'csi-pai-r19' occupies CPU(s) from the first symbol of the latest consecutive periodic/semi-persistent CSI-RS occasion of a corresponding linked CSI report (linked by inferenceReportConfigId-r19) no later than CSI reference resource of the linked CSI report, until the last symbol of the PUSCH carrying the CSI-PAI report. ============================= unchanged parts are omitted ============================ |

Reason for change: A new RRC IE CSI-LoggedMeasurementConfig is defined in 38.331 for network-side data collection, which is used to configure UE to perform the logging of measurements on CSI-RS resources. For CSI-RS measurement configured by the IE CSI-ReportConfig for L1 CSI report, there are some descriptions and constraints in spec 38.214, which are also needed for CSI-RS measurement configured by the IE CSI-LoggedMeasurementConfig for L3 CSI report.
Summary of change: Add descriptions and constraints for CSI-RS measurement configured by the IE CSI-LoggedMeasurementConfig (L3 CSI report) in 38.214.
Consequences if not approved: The descriptions and constraints for CSI-RS measurement configured by the IE CSI-LoggedMeasurementConfig (L3 CSI report) are missing in 38.214.
| 5.1.6.1.2 CSI-RS for L1-RSRP and L1-SINR computation If a UE is configured with a NZP-CSI-RS-ResourceSet configured with the higher layer parameter repetition set to 'on', the UE may assume that the CSI-RS resources, described in Clause 5.2.2.3.1, within the NZP-CSI-RS-ResourceSet are transmitted with the same downlink spatial domain transmission filter, where the CSI-RS resources in the NZP-CSI-RS-ResourceSet are transmitted in different OFDM symbols. If repetition is set to 'off', the UE shall not assume that the CSI-RS resources within the NZP-CSI-RS-ResourceSet are transmitted with the same downlink spatial domain transmission filter. The following changes for Clause 9.2 in TS 38.213 is endorsed.
The corresponding CR for Rel-19, TS 38.213 in R1-2606868 is endorsed.
- Reason for change: In Rel-19, UEIRI is introduced as a new type of UCI for notifying (ModeA) or requesting a PUSCH resource (ModeB) for UE-initiated/event-driven beam reporting. Whether UE transmits UEIRI on a PUCCH format 0 or format 1 in the PUCCH resource depends on whether the triggering condition of the event(s) for UE-initiated/event-driven beam reporting is met or not. In this case, the information bit of UEIRI is not always included in the PUCCH resource. However, in the current spec, UEIRI is described as a compulsory UCI in the PUCCH resource, which is not correct.
- Summary of change: Add the condition “if any” to the information bit for UEIRI where the contents of UCI bit(s) are described in the first paragraph of Section 9.2, TS38.213.
- Consequences if not approved: The availability of information bit for UEIRI in PUCCH is not correctly stated.
| 9.2 UCI reporting in physical uplink control channel UCI types reported in a PUCCH include HARQ-ACK information, SR, LRR, UEIRI, and CSI. UCI bits include HARQ-ACK information bits, if any, SR information bits, if any, LRR information bit, if any, UEIRI information bit, if any, and CSI bits, if any. The HARQ-ACK information bits correspond to a HARQ-ACK codebook as described in clause 9.1. For the remaining of this clause, unless stated otherwise in clauses 9.2.4A and 9.2.5.1, any reference to SR is applicable for SR and/or for LRR and/or for UEIRI. <Unchanged parts are omitted> |

| Reason for change: | In NB-IoT NTN TDD operation, it was concluded to do not “specify further enhancements for NPUSCH format 1 scheduling delays”. This was adopted based on the understanding that legacy scheduling values (8, 16, 32, 64) can be used under the assumption that if the scheduled uplink transmission falls into a guard period subframe (muted subframe) then the most immediate available subframe is used. However, this assumption/behavior is currently not described into the 3GPP technical specifications. |
|  |  |
| Summary of change: | Incorporating in clause 16.5.1 of TS 36.213 for NB-IoT NTN TDD operation, a statement that aligns terminology of legacy procedures (i.e., “a slot is considered an NB-IoT UL slot if is it fully contained within an NB-IoT UL subframe”) to reflect that if because of the scheduling delay value the NPUSCH format 1 transmission happens to coincide with a guard period subframe, then the NPUSCH format 1 transmission shall be performed at the first available subframe of the U consecutive uplink subframes of NB-IoT NTN TDD operation. |
|  |  |
| Consequences if not approved: | If the behavior is not described, there is no guarantee that all implementations will have to assume that a scheduled uplink transmission that falls into a guard period subframes should be understood to be postponed to the most immediate available uplink subframe. |

The misalignment between transmission of PRACH at UE side and monitoring of PRACH at NW side may occur in beam hopping operation when RO periodicity is <160ms. Some companies have the view that the misalignment is due to configuration or NW implementation.
The misalignment may also occur in beam hopping operation when RO periodicity is 160ms and cells served by the same hopping beam have overlapping valid PRACH occasions, e.g. due to the aligned SFN and same PRACH time-domain configuration and SSB-to-RO mapping, while the corresponding satellite Rx beam is not active for a footprint at such PRACH occasions.

| Reason for change: | Current specification already reflects the agreed SBFD slot-counting behavior for CG PUSCH with TBoMS or PUSCH repetition type A with available slot counting in the within-slot case. However, the corresponding across-slot case remains restricted to DCI-scheduled PUSCH, resulting in inconsistent handling between the within-slot and across-slot cases and misalignment with the corresponding RAN1 agreements. |
|  |  |
| Summary of change: | For the case of PUSCH transmissions across SBFD symbols and non-SBFD symbols in different slots, remove ‘scheduled by DCI format 0_1, 0_2 or 0_3’ in ‘For PUSCH repetition type A scheduled by DCI format 0_1, 0_2 or 0_3 when AvailableSlotCounting is enabled and K>1 or TB processing over multiple slots’ to ensure consistent handling between the within-slot and across-slot cases and alignment with the corresponding RAN1 agreements. |
|  |  |
| Consequences if not approved: | Inconsistent handling between the within-slot and the across-slot cases and misalignment with the corresponding RAN1 agreements. |
| ==============First change============== 6.1.2.1a Resource allocation in time domain for SBFD For a UE scheduled with PUSCH transmission occasions across SBFD symbols and non-SBFD symbols in different slots, - if the UE is not configured with sbfd-Config2-Transmission, or if the UE is configured with sbfd-Config2-Transmission and for PUSCH transmissions scheduled by DCI format 0_0 with CRC scrambled by TC-RNTI or RAR UL grant and associated with a PRACH transmission in second PRACH occasions, - the UE transmits only the PUSCH in a valid symbol type; - For Type 1 PUSCH transmissions with a configured grant, the valid symbol type is provided by symbolType in rrc-ConfiguredUplinkGrant in ConfiguredGrantConfig. - For Type 2 PUSCH transmissions with a configured grant or PUSCH transmissions scheduled by DCI scrambled with SP-CSI-RNTI, the valid symbol type is the symbol type of the first PUSCH transmission occasion associated with activation DCI. For Type 2 PUSCH transmissions with a configured grant of PUSCH repetition type B, the valid symbol type is the symbol type of the first actual repetition associated with activation DCI. - For PUSCH transmissions scheduled by DCI format 0_1, 0_2, 0_3, or PUSCH transmissions scheduled by DCI format 0_0 with CRC scrambled by TC-RNTI, RAR UL grant and associated with a PRACH transmission in second PRACH occasions, the valid symbol type is the symbol type of the first PUSCH transmission occasion indicated by the scheduling DCI or the RAR UL grant. For PUSCH repetition type B scheduled by DCI format 0_1 or 0_2, the valid symbol type is the symbol type of the first actual repetition occasion indicated by scheduling DCI. The UE does not expect that the first PUSCH transmission occasion indicated by scheduling DCI or the RAR UL grant is mapped to both SBFD symbols and non-SBFD symbols, except for PUSCH repetition type B. - For PUSCH repetition type A scheduled by DCI format 0_1, 0_2 or 0_3 when AvailableSlotCounting is enabled and K>1 or TB processing over multiple slots or PUSCH repetition type A scheduled by DCI format 0_0 with CRC scrambled by TC-RNTI or RAR UL grant and associated with a PRACH transmission in second PRACH occasions, - a slot containing the transmission occasion that is not in the valid symbol type is not counted in the number of slots. - In case the valid symbol type is SBFD symbol, a slot is counted in the number of slots if the symbols allocated for the transmission occasion in the slot are all SBFD symbols and not include a symbol of an SS/PBCH block with index provided by ssb-PositionsInBurst. - In case the valid symbol type is non-SBFD symbol, if the PUSCH repetition type A is scheduled by DCI format 0_0 with CRC scrambled by TC-RNTI or RAR UL grant and associated with a PRACH transmission in second PRACH occasions, a slot is counted in the number of slots if the symbols allocated for the transmission occasion in the slot are all non-SBFD symbols and not include a DL symbol indicated by tdd-UL-DL-ConfigurationCommon, if provided, or a symbol of an SS/PBCH block with index provided by ssb-PositionsInBurst. Otherwise, a slot is counted in the number of slots if the symbols allocated for the transmission occasion in the slot are all non-SBFD symbols and not include a DL symbol indicated by tdd-UL-DL-ConfigurationCommon or tdd-UL-DL-ConfigurationDedicated, if provided, or a symbol of an SS/PBCH block with index provided by ssb-PositionsInBurst. - For PUSCH repetition type B, UE drops an actual repetition if the actual repetition is not in the valid symbol type. - otherwise, the UE transmits the PUSCH occasions in SBFD symbols and non-SBFD symbols after applying collision handling in clause 11.1 of [6, TS 38.213], if any. For PUSCH repetition type A scheduled by DCI format 0_1, 0_2 or 0_3 when AvailableSlotCounting is enabled and K>1 or TB processing over multiple slots, a slot is counted in the number of slots if the symbols allocated for the transmission occasion in the slot are all SBFD symbols and not include a symbol of an SS/PBCH block with index provided by ssb-PositionsInBurst, or the symbols allocated for the transmission occasion in the slot are all non-SBFD symbols and not include a DL symbol indicated by tdd-UL-DL-ConfigurationCommon or tdd-UL-DL-ConfigurationDedicated, if provided, or a symbol of an SS/PBCH block with index provided by ssb-PositionsInBurst. For a UE configured with SBFD symbols and scheduled with a PUSCH transmission occasion that is mapped to SBFD symbols and non-SBFD symbols within a slot, - If the PUSCH transmission occasion is scheduled for PUSCH repetition type A with AvailableSlotCounting is enabled and K>1 or TB processing over multiple slots, or the PUSCH transmission is scheduled by DCI format 0_0 with CRC scrambled by TC-RNTI or RAR UL grant and associated with a PRACH transmission in a second PRACH occasion, the slot is not counted in the number of slots. - If the PUSCH transmission occasion is a nominal repetition for PUSCH repetition type B, the nominal repetition is segmented into actual repetitions around boundary of SBFD symbols and non-SBFD symbols. If the UE is not configured with sbfd-Config2-Transmission, UE drops an actual repetition if the actual repetition is not in the valid symbol type. - Otherwise, the UE does not transmit the PUSCH transmission occasion. <unchanged texts omitted> ==============End of change============== |

For Rel-20 LBCA via switching, in terms of interpretation of configured new Rel-20 switching pattern
- For a bit value of ‘0’ for a first slot in the bitmap, keep the same interpretation as Rel-19, i.e., UE can transmit/receive on the PCell in the first slot.
- For a bit value of ‘1’ for a second slot in the bitmap, change the interpretation, i.e., UE can receive on both the SCell and the PCell simultaneously in the second slot and cannot transmit on the PCell.

- Introduce new RRC parameter for Rel-20 LBCA via switching including a switching pattern, a gap duration for switching from PCell UL to SCell DL, and gap duration for switching from SCell DL to PCell UL.
  - The value range of each RRC parameter in Rel-20 LBCA via switching configuration is the same as the value range of the corresponding parameter in Rel-19 LBCA via switching configuration.
  - ‘0’ in the switching pattern indicates operation on FDD DL/UL carrier (PCell) only
  - ‘1’ in the switching pattern indicates dual-DL operation on FDD DL carrier + SDL carrier (SCell)
- A UE cannot be configured simultaneously with both the Rel-19 LBCA via switching and the Rel-20 LBCA via switching.
- The same as Rel-19, no UE feature related to Rel-20 LBCA via switching is expected in RAN1

For Rel-20 LBCA via switching, in terms of collision handling, when Rel-20 LBCA via switching is configured, only the following modification to the existing Rel-19 LBCA via switching collision is needed
- UE can receive SS/PBCH block, PDSCH, or PDCCH, or CSI-RS, or PRS configured by higher layers on the PCell in a set of symbols of a slot with bit value ‘1’, unless the set of symbols includes at least one symbol that is in the second duration.

entries.text:
For further study of initial access for idle mode multi-carrier operation, consider at least the following potential use cases:
  - UC-1: UL coverage enhancement / DL-UL coverage imbalance
  - UC-2: RACH capacity / offloading / load balancing
  - UC-3: Network energy saving / common-signaling reduction
  - Other use cases are not precluded.
  - For each identified use case, study whether and under which conditions multiple-carrier operation in idle mode provides additional benefit over existing mechanisms.

For study of multiple carriers where for initial access a UE can utilize resources for UL (Msg1, etc) or for both UL (Msg1, etc.) and DL (Msg2, etc.) in one carrier other than the carrier where the UE obtains the system information providing configuration for those resources, consider the following potential scenarios for the set of candidate physical carriers for which resources are provided for initial access:
  - S1: 1 DL physical carrier + N UL physical carriers, where N > 1
  - S2: M DL physical carriers + 1 UL physical carrier, where M > 1
  - S3: M DL physical carriers + N UL physical carriers, where M > 1 and N > 1
Note 1: The carrier where the UE obtains the system information and other candidate physical carrier(s) are counted above.
Note 2: For a given UE and a given initial access procedure, UE may use only a subset of the candidate physical carrier.
Note 3: The inclusion of a scenario for study does not imply agreement to support it. The need and applicable use cases/deployment scenarios for each scenario are subject to further study.

For study of multiple carriers where for initial access a UE can utilize resources for UL (Msg1, etc) or for both UL (Msg1, etc.) and DL (Msg2, etc.) in one carrier other than the carrier where the UE obtains the system information providing configuration for those resources,
  - As a baseline, a single selected physical carrier is used per link direction throughout an attempt of an RACH procedure.

For further study of multiple carriers where for initial access a UE can utilize resources for UL (Msg1, etc) or for both UL (Msg1, etc.) and DL (Msg2, etc.) in one carrier other than the carrier where the UE obtains the system information providing configuration for those resources, consider at least the following deployment conditions:
  - D1: co-located carriers for which a common timing/frequency synchronization relationship can be assumed
  - D2: co-located carriers for which a common timing/frequency synchronization relationship cannot be assumed
  - D3: non-collocated carriers for which a common timing/frequency synchronization relationship cannot be assumed
  - Other relevant deployment assumptions, including carrier frequency relationship / band separation, numerology / duplexing configuration and UE RF/baseband capability, are considered as applicable.
Note: whether a common timing/frequency synchronization relationship can be assumed is from UE perspective.

Study UL transmission switching across carriers in 6GR, at least considering the following:
- Whether/how to achieve unified design for all UL signals/channels
- Signaling for switching, e.g., dynamic and/or semi-static switching
- Number of Tx chains
- Number of carriers
- Switching gap
- Interaction with carrier aggregation operation
- Coordination with other WG(s), e.g., RAN4 (as needed)
- Note: SRS antenna switching is separately discussed under UL CSI agenda

Study DL reception switching across carriers in 6GR, at least considering the following:
- Applicable scenario(s) (e.g., the scenario(s) considered for NR LB-CA), including identify the scenario(s)
- Coordination with other WG(s), e.g., RAN4 (as needed)

For 6GR multiple carrier operation in connected mode, study mechanisms for fast enabling/disabling access to additional carriers, considering at least the following:
- UE power saving and/or NW energy saving
- Carrier states
- How to enable/disable
- Assumed NW-side requirements/conditions
- Assumed UE-side requirements

For 6GR multiple carrier operation in connected mode, study mechanisms for PXSCH resource allocation, considering at least the following:
- A PXSCH confined within a carrier
- A PXSCH over multiple carriers
  - Applicable scenario and condition
  - Coordination with other WG(s), e.g., RAN4 (as needed)

For 6GR multiple carrier operation in connected mode, study mechanisms for scheduling PXSCH, considering at least the following:
- Self-carrier scheduling
  - Note: self-carrier scheduling is that a DCI on a carrier schedules a PXSCH on a same carrier
- Cross-carrier scheduling
  - Note: cross-carrier scheduling is that a DCI on a carrier schedules a PXSCH on another carrier
- Multi-carrier scheduling
  - Note: multi-carrier scheduling is that a DCI on a carrier schedules a single PXSCH across multiple carriers, or individual PXSCH per carrier
- Coordination with other WG(s), e.g., RAN4 (as needed)
- Applicable scenario and condition for the above mechanism(s)
- Multiple slot scheduling will be discussed separately in other agenda.

For the study of bandwidth operation with single carrier operation in CONNECTED mode for a UE in 6G, at least consider the following:
- A “6GR-BW” should comprise at least a frequency location and the number of contiguous PRBs within a carrier.
  - Study the necessity that any other parameter (s) are associated to a “6GR-BW” operation
    - Note: RAN1 strives to minimize the number of parameter(s) that is associated with a “6GR-BW”
- Signal(s)/channel(s) transmission/receiving associated to a “6GR-BW”
- Benefit(s) and necessity of switching of “6GR-BW” for DL and/or UL, and potential mechanisms for switching

For the link budget evaluations in around 7 GHz for coverage gap identification, the assumptions for the receiver noise figure are 9 dB and 5 dB for DL and UL respectively (agreed in RAN1#124)
- Send an LS to RAN4 about the assumptions for information only.

For the link budget evaluations for the coverage gap identification, no update to the cell area reliability for initial-access related signals/channels, i.e., 95% for control channel, SSB and SIB1 and 90% for other channels that are capable of HARQ retransmissions but HARQ retransmissions are not assumed.
Support Resource block boundaries alignment between NR and 6GR on a MRSS carrier.
In 6GR, aNB-side semi-static SBFD is supported.

For 6GR, one SSB is defined by a single value of X
- One 6GR SSB spans X (4<=X<=7) OFDM symbols within a slot
- One 6GR SSB spans 20 RBs
For one 6G SSB, the number of RBs for PSS is 12 RBs.

Study the following aspects for 6GR PSS
- Sequence type
  - Option 1: m-sequence
  - Option 2: ZC-based sequence
  - Option 3: Other sequence
- Sequence length
  - Option 1: 127
  - Option 2: 127<L<=144
- Number of sequences
- Number of symbols for PSS

Study the following aspect for 6GR SSS
- Sequence type
  - Gold sequence as a benchmark
  - FFS: Other sequences
- Sequence length
  - Option 1: 127
  - Option 2: > 127
- Number of sequences
- Number of symbols for SSS

RAN1 to study and evaluate the following solutions
- Option 1:
  - SSB repetition within one SSB period and UE is assumed to at least support SSB combining within one SSB period
  - 160 ms default SSB periodicity for initial cell search
- Option 2:
  - SSB repetition within one SSB period and UE is assumed to at least support SSB combining within one SSB period
  - 80 ms default SSB periodicity for initial cell search
- Option 3:
  - UE is assumed to at least support SSB combining across different SSB periods
  - 40 ms default SSB periodicity for initial cell search
- Option 4:
  - SSB repetition within one SSB period and UE is assumed to at least support SSB combining within one SSB period and support SSB combining across different SSB periods
  - 40 ms default SSB periodicity for initial cell search
- Option 5:
  - UE is assumed to at least support SSB combining across different SSB periods
  - 20 ms default SSB periodicity for initial cell search
To mitigate the UE impact with longer SSB periodicity in Option 1/2/3/4, RAN1 to study the following solutions
- Solutions to reduce cell search complexity and latency
- Additional synchronization signals
- Clustered allocations of SSB, SIB1 and paging
- Other solutions are not precluded
FFS: Additional configurable SSB periodicities

To report the following details for PRACH evaluations:
- Receiver algorithm details, including:
  - Detection threshold strategy:
    - threshold configured to address false alarm only (impacting miss detection)
      - Example 1) Threshold is determined based on noise variance
    - threshold configured to address false alarm (impacting miss detection) and false detection probability jointly
      - Example 2) Threshold is determined based on noise variance, inter-sequence interference + noise estimated from measurements outside the window of the detected peak
        - Detection metric is normalized by interference+noise estimate, where the estimate is derived (e.g., maximum or median of the detection metric) from the detection metric outside the window around the detected peak within the NCS duration of the preamble. The detection peak window can be +/- estimated/approximated channel delay.
      - Example 3) Threshold is determined based on noise variance, sequence interference estimated from measurement of total receive signal power of a RO
  - In case of ZC sequence detection with Restricted Set A and B, details of detection algorithm to handle the detection sidelobes.
- For False alarm statistics, which option used for false alarm (and determination of detection threshold)
  - Option 1) if BS performs detection on a RO, the false alarm event happens for a preamble sequence detection, and a false alarm event is counted for the preamble sequence (false alarm event may happen multiple times within a RO for across the multiple preamble sequences). In this case, the denominator used to compute false alarm probability is the number of preambles to be detected (per RO).
  - Option 2) if BS performs detection on a RO, the false alarm event happens for any preamble sequence detection, and the a single false alarm event counted for a RO. In this case, denominator used to compute false alarm probability is 1 (per RO).
- Relative Tx power assumption of UEs (and any pathloss measurement and RF impairment modeling, if used)
- User distribution per RO, for example
  - Same number of users transmitting PRACH preamble in each RO
  - Varying number of users transmitting PRACH preamble in each RO (may be based on traffic characteristics)
- Preamble sequence selection
  - For example, NR ZC provides information on number of root sequences, number of cyclic shifts, and Ncs value among the 64 preamble set used for evaluation.

For study of whether the maximum number of preambles per RO is increased beyond 64, take into account at least:
- the justification and use case for the capacity increase (e.g., load model, access rate per cell, target collision probability, availability of ROs in time/frequency);
- the available root-sequence pool and the resulting inter-cell reusing for the assumed sequence length; and

  - Excess granted resource caused by buffer size quantization.
- Study and evaluate the required/maximal bit size and study the quantization method.
- With the same aggregated UL resource overhead of multi-bit SR and 1-bit SR+ scheduled PUSCH for BSR, evaluate UL transmission scheduling latency performance of multi-SR vs the mechanism of 1-bit SR + BSR (the waiting time for next SR transmission occasion is included).
- Evaluate the link coverage of multi-bit SR transmission in PUCCH with 1-bit SR coverage as baseline.
- Compare the multi-bit SR carrying quantized buffer size with the solution of using multiple 1-bit SR configurations to indicate the same target quantized buffer size, considering the resource overhead and UL transmission scheduling latency.
- Other candidate reporting contents can also be evaluated
  - E.g., delay status report, LCH/LCG ID, predicted traffic timing information.

entries.agenda_title: Other physical layer signals, channels and procedure
entries.text:
For remote interference management for 6GR:
- At least support wireless-based RIM framework specified in 5G/NR as starting point for 6GR.
  - Further study whether to support backhaul-based RIM framework.
- Support the following two types of RIM-RS:
  - RIM-RS Type 1: transmitted by victim BS to indicate the existence of remote interference
  - RIM-RS Type 2: transmitted by aggressor BS to detect if remote interference still exists.
  - The RIM RS shall carry the following information:
    - BS group ID
    - ‘Enough/Not enough’ indication in RIM-RS Type 1
    - ‘Near/Far’ indication in RIM RS type 1.
    - FFS: the RIM RS can carry 6G specific information.
    - FFS: the RIM RS to carry duplex specific information, e.g., TDD frame structure, SBFD  subband/symbol configuration.
  - FFS the time-domain and frequency domain design of RIM RS, the sequence in RIM RS, and the configuration methods of RIM RS, time location of RIM RS.
  - FFS whether CSI-RS can be reused as RIM RS.
ffs: FFS: the RIM RS can carry 6G specific information.
FFS: the RIM RS to carry duplex specific information, e.g., TDD frame structure, SBFD  subband/symbol configuration.
FFS the time-domain and frequency domain design of RIM RS, the sequence in RIM RS, and the configuration methods of RIM RS, time location of RIM RS.
FFS whether CSI-RS can be reused as RIM RS.

entries.agenda_title: Other physical layer signals, channels and procedure
entries.text:
For BS-to-BS CLI handling in 6GR, recommend to support information exchange between BSs and study the following candidate information exchange content:
- The slot configuration in TDD and time/frequency configuration of SBFD.
- The configuration of BS-to-BS CLI measurement RS: CSI-RS and/or 6GR SSB.
- The BS-to-BS CLI measurement results.
- DL Tx beam(s) information.
- Recommended and non-recommended beam.
- BS-to-BS CLI mitigation request.

entries.agenda_title: Other physical layer signals, channels and procedure
entries.text:
Study UE-initiated UE-to-UE CLI (UEI CLI) reporting with considering the following details:
- The definition of CLI event is: when at least one RSRP/RSSI measurement larger than a configured threshold for a given time length, the CLI event is triggered.
  - FFS: other CLI-related event(s).
- Study and determine the measurement metric for CLI event detection:
  - Option 1: non-filtered L1-RSRP/L1-RSSI
  - Option 2: filtered L1-RSRP/L1-RSSI.
- Study the CLI event detection procedure, report procedure and report contents.
ffs: FFS: other CLI-related event(s).

entries.agenda_title: Other physical layer signals, channels and procedure
entries.text:
For UE-to-UE CLI measurement in 6GR, the followings are recommended:
- Support RSRP and RSSI as the measurement metrics
  - Wideband RSSI measurement is supported.
  - FFS on subband RSSI measurement.
- Support to use SRS for RSRP measurement
- Support to use CLI RSSI measurement resource for RSSI measurement
  - For SBFD, UE measures the UE-to-UE CLI in UL subband
- FFS: For SBFD, whether the UE can measure CLI in UL subband in the time duration of DL reception.
- FFS: whether the UE measures the UE-to-UE CLI in DL subband in SBFD.
ffs: FFS on subband RSSI measurement.
FFS: For SBFD, whether the UE can measure CLI in UL subband in the time duration of DL reception.
FFS: whether the UE measures the UE-to-UE CLI in DL subband in SBFD.

entries.agenda_title: Other physical layer signals, channels and procedure
entries.text:
For UE-to-UE CLI reporting in 6GR, study L1 network-controlled CLI reporting with considering the followings:
- Study The latency requirement for CLI reporting to determine the necessity of L1 network-controlled CLI reporting.
- Consider periodic, semi-persistent and aperiodic reporting.
  - Study the applicable scenarios for each reporting mechanism.
- Consider the following two reporting content options:
  - Option 1: N strongest RSRP or RSSI and corresponding resource indicators. The UE reports RSRP/RSSI for the strongest one and differential RSRP/RSSI for the other N-1.
  - Option 2: a bit-map reporting with each bit corresponding each measurement resource, and bit value = 1 indicating the RSRP/RSSI measurement is above a configured threshold.
  - Study the benefit of each reporting content.
- Further study the following additional reporting content:
  - UE reports the time information corresponding to the measurement resource with the largest RSRP/RSSI measurement.

entries.agenda_title: Other physical layer signals, channels and procedure
entries.text:
Study non-transparent PUSCH resource muting mechanism for handling BS-to-BS CLI in 6GR and at least consider the following aspects:
- The muting mechanism specified in NR rel-19 is the starting point for study.
- Pattern(s) of resource muting.
  - Including study whether/how to support flexible muting patterns for resource efficiency.
- Whether/how to support dynamic/flexible adjustment of symbol position of muting resource.
- Whether/how to support dynamic disable/enable muting.
- Whether/how the TBS determination should consider the muting pattern in one PUSCH transmission.
- Whether/how same symbol power can be maintained between muting and non-muting
- Impact of multiplexed UCI in PUSCH
- Performance comparison between non-transparent and transparent PUSCH resource muting mechanism.

entries.agenda_title: Design of WUS with OFDM based sequence
entries.text: Study DL WUS for both basic coverage and extended coverage.

entries.agenda_title: Design of WUS with OFDM based sequence
entries.text:
- For DL WUS evaluations in FR1 and ~7 GHz, RAN1 assumes 1 µs and 2 ppm for maximum timing and frequency errors, Temax and Femax, respectively, prior to detecting DL WUS, at least within the same carrier as SSB.
- Consider additionally potential solutions when necessary for addressing 2 µs timing error and 5 ppm frequency error, e.g.,
  - DL WUS processing timeline relaxation
- The actual timing and frequency errors, Te and Fe, respectively, are modelled as uniform distributions, Te ~ U [-Temax, Temax ] µs and Fe ~ U [-Femax, Femax] ppm, respectively, are assumed for link level simulations.

entries.agenda_title: Design of WUS with OFDM based sequence
entries.text: RAN1 to down select between Zadoff-Chu sequence family and Gold sequence family for DL WUS at latest by RAN1#127.

entries.agenda_title: Design of WUS with OFDM based sequence
entries.text:
Study maximum number of transmittable sequence candidates and maximum number of sequence candidates targeting a UE per DL WUS sequence resource, considering, e.g.,
- Detection performance
- UE complexity and energy consumption
- Overhead
- BS complexity
- Resilience to neighbor cell interference
- RRC states
- Information provided by DL WUS
- Basic and extended coverage
Note: A DL WUS sequence resource is the time and frequency resource of a single WUS sequence. A DL WUS MO may include multiple DL WUS sequence resources, including the same or different sequence.

entries.agenda_title: Design of WUS with OFDM based sequence
entries.text:
- 1% BLER of the reference PDCCH at -8.1 dB SNR is assumed as the starting point of DL WUS design.
  - Further discussed extended coverage.

At least in RRC idle, study for 6GR DL WUS by considering
- At least SSB is used as QCL source, the association between SSB and DL WUS monitoring occasion(s), and the QCL type(s)

For RRC connected, study feasibility and necessity of serving cell RLM measurement by EE processing, considering at least:
- UE energy saving gain
- Coverage (e.g., achievable SINR/SNR) and accuracy
  - Measurement metrics
- Impact on the EE processing complexity
- Based on at least 6GR sync signal
  - other signals
- Whether there is spec impact or not

Study the following cases for 6GR DL WUS monitoring occasions:
- Case 1: A set of WUS monitoring occasions associated with at least one PO for a UE are TDMed, multiple sets of WUS monitoring occasions are TDMed.
- Case 2: A set of WUS monitoring occasions associated with at least one PO for a UE are TDMed, multiple sets of WUS monitoring occasions are FDMed or FDMed combined with TDMed.
- Case 3: A set of WUS monitoring occasions associated with at least one PO for a UE are FDMed or FDMed combined with TDMed
For case 1, 2, and 3, UE is not required to monitor more than one MO at given time.
considering at least:
- Impact on the UE energy consumption
- Impact on the UE complexity
- Network energy gains if any

For collection of UE energy saving gain results for 6GR DL WUS in RRC connected, at least the following cases are considered:
- Case 1:No neighboring cell RRM measurement
| Case | Schemes for triggering PDCCH monitoring | Serving cell RLM/RRM measurement | Neighboring cell RRM measurement |
| Case1-1 | C-DRX only | Non-EE processing | Not applicable |
| Case1-2 | C-DRX with DCP | Non-EE processing | Not applicable |
| Case 1-3 | C-DRX with DL WUS | Non-EE processing | Not applicable |
| Case 1-4 | C-DRX with DL WUS | EE processing | Not applicable |
| Case 1-5 | DL WUS | Non-EE processing | Not applicable |
| Case 1-6 | DL WUS | EE processing | Not applicable |
- Case 2: with neighboring cell RRM measurement
| Case | Schemes for triggering PDCCH monitoring | Serving cell RLM/RRM measurement | Neighboring cell RRM measurement |
| Case 2-1 | C-DRX only | Non-EE processing | non-EE processing |
| Case 2-2 | C-DRX with DCP | Non-EE processing | non-EE processing |
| Case 2-3 | C-DRX with DL WUS | Non-EE processing | non-EE processing |
| Case 2-4 | C-DRX with DL WUS | EE processing | Non-EE processing |
| Case 2-5 | C-DRX with DL WUS | EE processing | EE processing |
| Case 2-6 | DL WUS | Non-EE processing | non-EE processing |
| Case 2-7 | DL WUS | EE processing | Non-EE processing |
| Case 2-8 | DL WUS | EE processing | EE processing |
Note 1: Neighboring cell RRM measurement includes at least intra-frequency measurement, inter-frequency measurement is up to company report. How neighboring cell RRM measurement is performed by EE processing is up to companies’ report, including power consumption. L1 measurement is up to companies’ report.
Note 2: For traffic, FTP, XR, IM can be evaluated and traffic arrvival rate is up to companies’ report
Note 3: Assumed sleep state is up to company report.
Note 4: In this evaluation, no further power scaling based on the number of occupied SSB symbols within a slot for the measurement by EE processing
Note 5: If RLM/RRM measurement is not evaluated, please report.
Note 6: it’s up to companies’ report how the evaluated C-DRX different from NR C-DRX
Note 7: it’s up to companies’ report how the evaluated DCP different from NR DCP
Note 8: when comparing different cases, companies are encouraged to at least consider the same monitoring periodicity of 6GR DL WUS and C-DRX cycle. Other periodicities are up to companies’ report.

For collecting UE energy saving results for 6GR DL WUS:
- Endorse the template for collecting UE energy saving results in R1-2606878.
Email discussion for collecting UE energy saving results in RRC idle by 2nd Oct, including potential updates to the template if any.
Email discussion for collecting UE energy saving results in RRC connected by 6th Nov.

- For feasibility study of DS#1b, further study the following mechanisms for UE to acquire UL WUS configuration.
  - Option 1: Pre-configuration and/or pre-defined in specification
  - Option 2: Synchronization signal(s)
  - Option 3: PBCH including PBCH DMRS
  - Option 4: Broadcast PDSCH
  - Option 5: Common PDCCH
  - Note: Combination of above options can be considered.
  - At least the followings are considered for further study of the above options
    - NW configuration flexibility
    - NW and UE energy saving/consumption
    - UE complexity
    - Signaling overhead
    - Necessary payload by taking SIB26 for NR OD-SIB1 as the reference

- For study of necessity for UL WUS, at least followings are considered as candidates of use cases.
  - For UEs in idle mode,
    - UE-initiated on-demand or adaptation procedures for one or multiple of the following signals/channels:
      - 6GR SS/PBCH
      - 6GR SIB1
      - 6GR PRACH
      - 6GR DL Reference Signal
  - For UEs in connected mode,
    - UE-initiated on-demand or adaptation procedures for one or multiple of the following signals/channels:
      - 6GR SS/PBCH
      - 6GR SIB1
      - 6GR PRACH
      - 6GR DL Reference Signal
    - UL data indication (including ‘no UL data’ indication)
    - Selection of PUSCH resource and/or PUSCH transmission parameter
    - UL WUS based measurement
    - Indication of new beam for BFR (if supported for 6GR)
- With consideration of at least the following aspects:
  - 6GR SSB/SIB1 periodicity/repetition
  - Coverage
  - UL WUS detection performance
  - NW and UE energy/power consumption
  - Latency
  - NW and UE complexity
  - Resource overhead
  - Necessity of UE-triggered operation compared to NW-triggered mechanisms
  - Which DS(s) are applicable to the above use cases
  - Interference aspects
  - Inter-node coordination
  - Overlapping with existing or other 6GR mechanisms that could play the same functionalities

- For study of feasibility for UL WUS, followings are observed for DS#2a in addition to previous RAN1 agreement.
  - If UE transmits UL WUS to cell/carrier #2, and if cell/carrier #1 and cell/carrier #2 are non-co-located,
    - UE can determine UL WUS transmission power as the pre-defined TX power (e.g., maximum TX power) Further study
      - Whether/how to mitigate interference to the cell/carrier other than cell/carrier #2
      - Whether/how to handle the impact to UL WUS detection performance
      - Whether UE can determine path-loss estimation from cell/carrier #1 DL signals and power offset value provided by cell/carrier #1 when available/applicable.
        - Details on how to use path-loss estimation from cell/carrier #1 DL signals
    - UE can use wide/omni-directional beam or beam sweeping as UL WUS transmission beam. Further study
      - How to handle the impact of reduced cell coverage, when using wide/omni-directional beam.
      - How to determine narrow beam and whether/how to mitigate interference to the cell/carrier other than cell/carrier #2.
    - UE can use cell/carrier #1 SSB as timing reference for UL WUS transmission when cell/carrier #1 and cell/carrier #2 are synchronized when the timing can be maintained in UE, or when cell#1/carrier #1 provides underlay coverage for cell#2/carrier #2.
    - It is required to further study whether/how UE can use cell/carrier #1 SSB as timing reference for UL WUS transmission or not, when cell/carrier #1 and cell/carrier #2 are not synchronized, considering inter-cell distance, timing advance, etc.
    - This can cover the scenario where UE moves from cell/carrier #1 to cell/carrier #2 (where cell/carrier #1 may not provide underlay coverage for cell/carrier #2) and can maintain DL timing/frequency synchronization and UL WUS configuration for a certain period of time
      - It is required to further study the duration of the certain period of time with coordination with RAN4 as needed

- RAN1 to study necessary information and required payload size for UL WUS configuration, considering at least the following information and its necessity
  - Time and frequency domain resource size and location of UL WUS
  - Mapping between 6GR synchronization signal and UL WUS occasion
  - Parameters to determine UL WUS transmission power
  - Parameters to determine UL WUS sequence/format
  - Parameters for UE monitoring of response to UL WUS
  - Cell access related information
  - Note: SIB26 for NR OD-SIB1 is taken as a reference
  - Note: The above does not preclude that some necessary information may be implicitly determined, without need of explicit payload

- For UEs in RRC_IDLE / RRC_INACTIVE state, RAN1 to study at least the following candidate additional functions for DL-WUS:
  - Candidate #1: SI-modification and/or ETWS-CMAS notification carried via DL WUS.
  - Candidate #2: Use DL-WUS as a trigger or indication for on-demand and/or additional RS and/or common signals/channels, if supported.
  - Candidate #3: Use DL-WUS to indicate PF/PO resources or RACH occasions that can be used.
  - Candidate #4: Study DL WUS to trigger Downlink Small Data Transmission (DL SDT) in inactive state, if supported.

For 6GR NTN GNSS-less/free/degraded PRACH, the differential time and frequency errors documented in TR 38.742 are taken as targets for the study with the addition of at least the following scenarios:
- S-band LEO-300
- Ka-band LEO-300
- FFS: details of these scenarios, including differential time/frequency errors
ffs: FFS: details of these scenarios, including differential time/frequency errors

entries.text:
For the 6GR NTN GNSS-less/free/degraded PRACH study:
- The study is conducted in common agenda item, taking into account the NTN requirements which are developed under NTN specific agenda item (i.e. AI 10.7.1.).
  - This does not preclude NTN specific adjustments to the common design if needed, which may be developed under NTN specific agenda item (i.e. AI 10.7.1) if the design from the common agenda item does not meet the NTN requirements.

For Rel-20 6G ISAC performance evaluation, for object detection and/or tracking, when data fusion from multiple sensing nodes/pairs is applied:
- Instead of using detected objects per sensing node/pair, the jointly determined object(s) fused from detected objects of multiple sensing nodes/pairs will be used for association between detected object(s) and true target(s), calculating MDP, FAP Type 2 and positioning/velocity accuracy.
- Companies to report the method/algorithm to obtain the jointly fused object(s) from detected objects of multiple sensing nodes/pairs.

For Rel-20 6G ISAC evaluation on SAC (sensing assisted communication), companies are encouraged to evaluate and report at least one of the following:
- Scope 1: Evaluate performance of sensing measurement/result, which will be used to assist communication;
- Scope 2: Evaluate performance of communication, with and without assistance of sensing measurement/result. The sensing measurement/result to assist communication can be:
  - Ideal sensing measurement/result
  - Non-ideal sensing measurement/result, and company to report how to model error/offset of non-ideal factors for non-ideal sensing measurement/result
  - Real sensing measurement/result, which is obtained from simulation
  - Note: companies to report which is used in their simulation.
For Rel-20 6G ISAC evaluation on SAC, for Scope 2:
- The communication use case(s) in AI 10.8.2 are encouraged
- Companies to report whether the location and/or velocity information of communication UE and/or TRP is needed or not in their SAC algorithm/mechanism
  - Note: this does not imply specifying exchange of location and/or velocity information between UE and TRP
- Companies to report the time-frequency resource cost due to sensing for SAC and necessary details on the definition of the time-frequency resource cost based on TR38.765 as starting point
  - Comparison with benchmark and benchmark details should also be reported as well as other necessary details if any
- Companies are encouraged to use communication-related performance metrics as agreed in communication agendas
- Companies are encouraged to use baseline/benchmark mechanism as agreed in communication agendas for comparison; Use of state-of-the-art mechanism without assistance of sensing measurement/result for comparison is not precluded
- Companies are encouraged to use additional communication-related evaluation assumptions (if necessary but not discussed/agreed in AI 10.8.1) as agreed in communication agendas
Note: How to draw conclusion/observation is a separate discussion.

For Rel-20 6G ISAC evaluation on SAC, for Scope 1, the following sensing measurement/results and corresponding performance metrics are considered:
- Delay/Doppler/angle/power/phase related information of the ISAC channel
  - Performance metric:
    - RMSE of delay of the path(s) used to assist communication
    - RMSE of Doppler the path(s) used to assist communication
    - RMSE of angles (one or more of AOD, ZOD, AOA, ZOA) of the path(s) used to assist communication
    - RMSE of power of the path(s) used to assist communication
      - FFS: details on the power of the path(s)
    - FFS: RMSE of phase of the path(s) used to assist communication
    - Companies to report how to select the path(s), how to derive RMSE from multiple paths and how such sensing measurement/result of the paths(s) is able to assist communication
    - Note: when evaluated, companies are not required to report every metric
- Enrivonment (large surface, wall) that reconstructed by sensing
  - Performance metric:
    - Mean value of absolute perpendicular distance from the sensed specular reflection point to the ground-truth plane
    - Mean value of absolute perpendicular distance from the ground truth specular reflection point to the reconstructed plane
    - Note: when evaluated, companies are not required to report every metric
  - EO type-2 should be modeled in the simulation in this case
Companies are not required to evaluate and report every sensing measurement/result.
Note: In Scope 1, the performance metrics for detecting object for the purpose of SAC are the same as those for object detection and/or tracking, and thus already included in Rel-20 6G ISAC object detection and/or tracking study.
Note 2: How to draw conclusion/observation is a separate discussion.
ffs: FFS: details on the power of the path(s)
FFS: RMSE of phase of the path(s) used to assist communication
